title: Purifying DNA from Agarose with Homemade Glass Milk
author: Joanne Kamens
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcefitbn

steps.title: Prepare Glass Powder
steps.instruction: Resuspend 400 g of glass powder in 800 ml double distilled (dd) H2O in a 2 liter flask with a stir bar and stir for 60 minutes.

steps.title: Collect Glass Fines
steps.instruction: Collect the fine particles from the glass powder suspension.

substeps.instruction: Remove and keep the supernatant by gentle pouring, leaving all settled glass.
Pellet the remaining glass in a centrifuge for 10 minutes at 6000 RPM.

steps.title: Clean Glass Fines with Acid
steps.instruction: Clean the glass fines using nitric acid in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 250 ml ddH2O.
Add Nitric Acid to a final concentration of 50%.
Bring the solution close to a boil (must be performed in a fume hood).
Allow the solution to cool.

steps.title: Generate Glass Stock Aliquots
steps.instruction: Wash and aliquot the glass for storage.

substeps.instruction: Pellet the glass (as previously described) and wash 6 times with ddH2O.
Check and ensure the pH is neutral (same as water).
Resuspend the pellet with an equal volume of ddH2O relative to the pellet volume.
Aliquot into 50 ul aliquots and store in the freezer to keep the glass suspended.

steps.title: Prepare NaI Binding Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare and store the NaI binding solution.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 90.8 g NaI and 1.5 g Na2SO4 in 100 ml ddH2O.
Filter the solution through Whatman No. 1 paper into a dark bottle.
Place a dialysis bag containing 0.5 g Na2SO4 into the bottle to maintain saturation.
Wrap the bottle in foil and store at 4C.
Periodically check for brown discoloration; replace the solution if it turns brown.

steps.title: Prepare Glass Milk Wash Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a wash solution consisting of 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 50% EtOH, and 10 mM Tris pH 7.5. Store at -20C or 4C.

steps.title: Bind DNA from Gel Slices
steps.instruction: Bind DNA from agarose gel slices to the glass powder.

substeps.instruction: Determine the weight of the gel slices.
Add 2 ml NaI solution per gram of gel.
Incubate at 37 C (or up to 50 C to speed up the process), mixing occasionally until the agarose is totally dissolved.

steps.title: Wash DNA-Bound Glass
steps.instruction: Wash the glass pellet to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Spin the suspension in a centrifuge for 5 seconds.
Remove and discard the supernatant using a micropipette.
Wash the pellet by resuspending in 250 ul NaI solution (or 10X volume of glass if larger).
Spin and resuspend to wash the pellet 2-3 times with Glass Milk Wash solution (approximately the same volume), removing supernatant gently with a micropipette.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Recover the purified DNA from the glass pellet.

substeps.instruction: Dry the pellet well by air drying for a short time and/or carefully using a Kimwipe to remove all residual liquid.
Resuspend the pellet in ddH2O or TE (> 10 microliter).
Elute DNA at 37 C for more than 5-10 minutes.
Spin for 1 minute in a microfuge and collect the eluted DNA in the supernatant.

steps.title: Purify DNA from Solution
steps.instruction: Follow an alternative binding procedure for DNA already in solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 volumes of NaI solution to the DNA.
Immediately add 1 microliter of glass slurry per microgram of DNA (or ~1 ul for smaller amounts).
Incubate the DNA/glass mixture on ice for 5 minutes, mixing occasionally.
Proceed with the washing and elution steps (as described in the gel purification process).
